title: Long-term changes in the metabolome among youth elite athletes in team sports: A study spanning two competitive seasons, including a pilot study on the relationship between metabolomic profiles and performance parameters
summary:
Metabolomics is an important method for studying the body’s adaptations to training, as it can capture both short-term responses to exercise and long-term changes. In youth competitive sports in particular, there is an increased risk of maladaptations if the balance between training and recovery is not maintained, which can lead to chronic fatigue and impaired performance development. While studies on short-term effects already exist, there is currently a lack of research covering the entire course of a competitive season. This research gap is particularly relevant for young athletes, as training, recovery, and development are closely interlinked. The goal is therefore to identify early metabolic markers for such maladaptations in order to enable preventive, health-oriented, and individually tailored training management. 
This study addresses these research gaps by systematically tracking metabolomic adaptations over the course of two full competitive seasons and examining their relationship, particularly with training and performance data. It is expected that training-induced changes in metabolism over the course of the season can be systematically linked to performance development and recovery capacity. Particular emphasis is placed on the significance of these changes for performance, individual stress tolerance, and the health stability of young athletes.

interventions.name: Youth athletes in team sports (e.g. basketball, handball etc.) are asked to provide biological samples (blood, saliva & stool) at four specific time points throughout the competitive season as well as to complete a standardized questionnaire on nutritional knowledge and sleep habits at each of these

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Active athletes in youth competitive team sports who regularly participate in training sessions and competitions
- Age: 14–18
- Female and male athletes
- Regular participation in team training and competitions for at least one year
- No specific restrictions regarding ethnic or sociodemographic characteristics
- Non-smokers
- Willingness to continue participating regularly in training and competitions during the study period
- No known chronic diseases or acute health problems that could interfere with participation in the study or the collection of metabolomic markers and performance data
- Written consent from participants and their legal guardians to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
- younger than 14 or older than 18 (exception: if the athlete turns 18 during the current competitive season or falls into three age groups in the respective sport)
- No experience or less than one year of experience in team training or competitive play
- Presence of chronic illnesses or acute health problems
- Presence of injuries
- Active smoking or documented smoking in the past
- Use of medications (e.g., anti-inflammatory drugs)
- Prolonged absence from training or competition during the study period (e.g., due to vacation commitments)
- Refusal to participate in the study
- Lack of written consent from participants or their legal guardians
- Refusal or unwillingness to undergo sample collection or to follow the study protocols
